name: Dash
summary: On a key, the unit bursts forward much faster than its normal pace: a quick lunge of a few body-lengths, or a sprint lasting a few seconds, along the way it faces or moves. It closes the last gap to a target, gets out of a losing fight or crosses open ground under fire; then the key recharges or a small stock refills, so a spent dash leaves the unit at its normal pace. The burst runs in a line the enemy can read, and slows, roots and stuns cut it short. In the charge variants the burst is also a hit: the unit knocks aside, runs over or pins what it meets and slams its target. A speed boost that costs health or heat is overclock-self, a jump over walls is leap, an instant hop is teleport, and an order to run home is retreat-to-base.
counterplay: Read the tell and step off the line: the burst runs straight, so sidestep it, or put a wall, a barrier or a heavy teammate in its path.
Slow, root or stun it: a slow shortens the burst, and a root or stun stops a charge where it stands.
Wait until the dash is spent, then commit: while the key recharges it can neither escape nor close the gap again.
Keep spacing so one charge can't hit several of you, and stay off the walls a pinning charge could smash you into.
Make the far end of the dash deadly: a charge that ends deep in your lines lands in your team's crossfire.

other_examples.unit: King Oni: Bull Rush (Empire of the Rising Sun)
other_examples.note: A giant battle walker's targeted charge on a long cooldown: it rushes at a chosen enemy at about twice its walking speed and rams it for a heavy blow, and the game's ability text has it flatten foes caught on the way. During the rush it can crush heavier units than it normally does. A beta patch made it speed up as it charges and shortened the charge; a later patch makes a King Oni that an enemy ray has shrunk blow itself up when it rams.

other_examples.note: A squad battle cry bought with munitions that makes the squad move faster for a short time; its cooldown only starts once the effect ends, and nothing slows the squad afterwards. Players use it to dash through machine-gun fire into cover or to get a grenadier onto a tank's engine, and with munitions to spare they spam it just to cross the map. In multiplayer it adds speed only; in the campaign it also lifts damage and accuracy a little.

other_examples.note: A locked-on charge: the hero picks an enemy anywhere on the map and charges at it with a large speed bonus, passing through everything; each enemy he passes and the target itself are bashed, stunned and knocked back. Stuns, roots, sleeps and forced movement cancel the charge, his allies see a marker over the target, and the cooldown starts only when the charge ends.

shooter_analogues.note: A tank hero's charge on a short cooldown: he rushes forward in a straight line much faster than he walks, can turn only a little and can stop by pressing again. The first enemy he hits is caught and carried; if the charge ends in a wall, that enemy takes a huge hit, while anyone else he runs into is knocked aside for a small one. He can carry only one enemy at a time.

A mech's boost on a very short cooldown: it flies the way it faces for up to a couple of seconds while the pilot steers and keeps shooting. Enemies it barrels into are knocked back and take a little damage, and slowing effects cut its speed.

A primed dash: the first press spends her single charge and, after a short wind-up, opens a window of a few seconds in which a second press dashes her a short way along her current heading, or straight ahead if she stands still. Other players see gusts round her legs while it is primed. The charge returns after two kills, not on a timer. Patches lengthened the wind-up, shortened the window and made concussion slow the dash by half.

A shield that lets the Demoman charge once its meter is full: a short burst of speed almost straight ahead, with turning capped by a patch. The first enemy he touches takes a bash that grows with the distance charged, and his next melee swing hits harder, up to a critical hit after a long charge. Starting a charge also clears burning, bleeding and similar effects, and the meter then refills over several seconds.

In a top-down team shooter, the tank brawler's super is an aimed charge: he runs along the aimed line, breaks the obstacles he hits, knocks back and hurts enemies on the way, and slows enemies close to where he stops. He can still be hurt during the charge, and knockback doesn't stop it, but a stun does. The super fills from damage he takes, and teammates use the gaps he breaks in walls to reach the enemy safe or to score.

player_translation.summary: One key throws the unit forward in a short, fast burst, to close in, break away or cross open ground. It runs along a line the enemy can read, and once spent it leaves the unit at its normal pace until it recharges. The charge variants make the burst a hit as well.
as_user: Press Space and you surge forward the way you are moving, or the way you face if you stand still: a lunge of a few body-lengths in a moment, or a few seconds of much higher speed in the sprint variant. Then the key recharges.
Use it to close the last stretch to a target, to break line of sight, to cross a fire lane or to get out of a losing fight.
Spend it going in and you have no way out: the skill is keeping it for the moment that decides the fight.
In the base version you can't fire during the brief lunge and can barely steer; the sprint and steered-boost variants let you keep steering.
With a charge variant the burst is your attack: line it up so it ends on your target and knocks the others on the line aside; a wall or a heavy target stops you short.
as_target: A dash has a short tell (an engine rev, a crouch, a flare) and a straight path, so you can sidestep or put something in the way.
Slows shorten it, and a root or a stun stops a charge where it stands.
Once it has dashed, the pip over it shows the key recharging: it can't escape, so that is when you commit.
Against a charge, step off its line, stay away from walls you could be pinned against, and don't bunch up.
teammates: A dasher opens fights by reaching the back line first, and teammates follow up while the enemy turns to face it.
It can bait: dash in to draw fire, then dash back into your own team's guns.
A charge breaks up a firing line and leaves enemies knocked about for teammates to finish; the wall-breaker variant also opens new routes through cover.
The other team keeps a root, a slow or a stun ready for the end of its dash.
controls: Space (the key-bound movement slot): dash the way you move, or the way you face when standing still. One counted key.
Sprint variant: Space starts a few seconds of extra speed; press again to end it early.
Charge variants: Space charges along the aim line, with little turning; pressing again cancels.
Steered-boost variant: hold Space to keep boosting and steer with the mouse; firing stays on left mouse.
Primed variant: the first press primes the dash, with a wind-up everyone can see; a second press within a short window dashes.
The universal keys work as on every unit.
feedback: A clear tell at the start (engine rev, dust kick, exhaust flare) and a streak or after-image along the path, readable from above.
Charges show their line on the ground during the wind-up, so the target can see where it will run.
A cooldown pip over the unit that nearby enemies can read, and a recharge ring on the user's HUD.
On a charge's impact: a heavy thud, knockback bursts, and a distinct sound when a stun cancels it.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS a charge is often a targeted order that runs the victim down by itself (the King Oni's Bull Rush; Dota 2's Spirit Breaker works the same way); here the player aims the line, and a locked-on charge is a variant with a visible lock and a warning to the target.
RTS charges sit on long cooldowns, as the Tempest Sphere's does; one player needs a short burst on a short recharge as a regular tool, while a charge with a heavy blow keeps a long one.

The Sphere and the King Oni crush what lies on their line; that works against computer squads but feels random to players, so a charge knocks soldiers aside and hurts them, and only large or huge chargers run over the smallest units, after a visible line.
Height and walls are hard to read from above: a dash stops at walls and ledges, and only the wall-breaker variant smashes through, and then only light cover that is marked as breakable.
Fast movement strains lag compensation: the server decides where a dash ends and what it hits, and clients draw it as a smooth streak.

team_play.notes: The plain dash is a personal tool, but it lets a unit open fights and bait enemies forward, and the charge variants knock enemies out of position for teammates or, in the wall-breaker variant, open routes the whole team uses; the other team answers it together with roots, slows and stuns.

notes: A timed speed impulse with a recharge or a stock; the sprint variant is a timed speed modifier.
Collision rules for where a dash ends: walls, ledges, water, other units and vehicles.
Charge variants add contact checks along the path, knockback, a carried target for the pinning charge and breakable cover for the wall-breaker, which raise them to medium.
Server authority and lag compensation for the start and end points, so a dash never ends inside a wall on another player's screen.
Interactions with slows, roots and stuns must be decided once: a slow shortens the burst, a root or stun ends it.
Escape on demand: on a short recharge it makes a unit very hard to pin down, so tune the recharge against the length of a typical fight.
A gap-closer next to a burst weapon kills before the target can react; the tell and the line are the counterweight.
Speed buffs stacked on top of a dash break movement assumptions, so total speed needs a cap.
Charge knockback chained with other displacement can lock a target down; give each target a short immunity to repeat knockback.
A straight streak is easy to show from above, but a lunge that lasts a fraction of a second can be missed in a busy fight without a tell and a trail.
Players must tell a plain dash from a charge that hits; give charges their own wind-up and ground line.

variants.name: Quick lunge
variants.summary: A burst of a few body-lengths that takes a fraction of a second, the way you move or face; it does nothing to what it passes and recharges quickly.

variants.name: Sprint
variants.summary: A few seconds of much higher speed with full steering; nothing changes afterwards, and the key then waits out a medium recharge.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes 2 Conscripts' Oorah!, Tempest Rising Sniper and Missile Trooper Sprint, StarCraft II Medivac's Ignite Afterburners, Red Alert 3 Uprising Grinder's Turbo-Charge

variants.name: Ramming charge
variants.summary: The burst is also the attack: it knocks aside and hurts what it meets on the way, large chargers run over smaller units, and it slams the first thing it can't pass, then stops.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Tempest Sphere's Tempest Engine, Red Alert 3 King Oni's Bull Rush, Overwatch D.Va's Boosters

adds_strengths.why: Its charge closes the gap and hits in one move, knocking aside or running over what lies on its line.

adds_weaknesses.why: The charge runs straight and ends at the first wall or heavy target, and a stun cancels it, so a wasted charge leaves it stranded until the key recharges.

counters.why: Soldiers on its line are knocked aside and hurt, and a large or huge charger runs them over.

variants.name: Pinning charge
variants.summary: The first enemy struck is caught and carried along and takes a heavy blow if the charge ends against a wall; others on the line are knocked aside, steering is poor, and pressing again cancels.

counters.why: It can pluck one soldier out of a group and smash it into a wall.

variants.name: Locked-on charge
variants.summary: Pick an enemy in sight and charge until you reach it, bashing anything you pass; the target is warned, a stun, root or sleep ends the charge, and the recharge starts only when it ends.
variants.seen_in: Dota 2 Spirit Breaker's Charge of Darkness, which can lock onto an enemy anywhere on the map

variants.name: Primed dash
variants.summary: Press once to prime it: after a short wind-up that enemies can see, you have a few seconds to dash once; the charge comes back from kills rather than on a timer.

variants.name: Shield charge
variants.summary: Charge almost straight ahead behind a shield or a heavy hull; the first enemy touched takes a bash that grows with the distance charged, the next melee strike lands harder, and starting the charge shakes off burning and similar effects.

variants.name: Wall-breaking charge
variants.summary: The charge smashes through light cover and props, leaving gaps the team can use, knocks enemies aside and slows those near where it stops; it can be shot the whole way, and knockback doesn't stop it, but a stun does.

adds_strengths.why: Its charge breaks through light cover and opens new routes for the whole team.

adds_weaknesses.why: It can be shot all along its charge, and a stun stops it halfway.

variants.name: Steered boost
variants.summary: Hold the key to keep boosting for up to a couple of seconds, turning as you go and still firing; enemies you bump into are pushed back a little.

variants.name: Untouchable dash
variants.summary: Nothing can hurt the unit during the dash, so it slips through a volley; the dash is short and its recharge long.
variants.seen_in: Dota 2 Faceless Void's Time Walk (invulnerable on the way)

adds_strengths.why: A burst of speed on a key closes the last gap to a target, breaks away from a losing fight or crosses open ground faster than its normal pace allows.

adds_weaknesses.why: The burst runs in a line the enemy can read and block, and once spent it leaves the unit at its normal pace until the key recharges.

counters.why: Shells that take a while to land on a point miss a unit that bursts out of the impact area.

countered_by.why: A root stops a dash or a charge where it stands and keeps it from bursting away; roots cancel Spirit Breaker's charge in Dota 2.
A slow cuts every burst short, as concussion slows Jett's dash by half in Valorant.
A stun interrupts a charge halfway, as it stops Bull's charge in Brawl Stars.

open_questions: Should a charge run over soldiers outright, as the Tempest Sphere and the King Oni do, or only knock them aside? (Recommended: knock aside and hurt; only large or huge chargers crush, after a visible line.)
May the user fire during a dash? (Recommended: not during the base lunge; the sprint and steered-boost variants may.)
One dash on a recharge, or a small stock of two that refills one at a time? A stock rewards skill but lengthens escapes.
May a plain dash be a card's signature? This file says any, because the charge variants can carry a card (the Tempest Sphere, Brawl Stars' Bull), but a plain sprint is better as an extra.

shooter_fit.reason: The most common movement verb in action and top-down shooters (Overwatch, Valorant, Brawl Stars); a straight streak with a tell reads well from above, it costs little to build, and the charge variants add team play. As a generic pattern it fills out cards more often than it defines them.
